chunks: that he who likens You with the separateness of the limbs of Your creation, and the joining of the extremities of their joints which are concealed for the management of Your wisdom, did not fix the unseen of his conscience upon knowledge of You, and certainty did not touch his heart to the effect that there is no rival for You,

and it is as though he has not heard the followers declaring themselves free of their followers when they say: 'By Allah, we were certainly in manifest error when we equalled you with the Lord of the worlds.'
ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha define true knowledge of God in contrast to physical anthropomorphism?
ai.summary: In the chapter of Al-Ashbaah, Imam Ali critiques anthropomorphism (Tashbih) by contrasting God's transcendent unity with the visible, composite nature of creation, arguing that physical resemblance implies limitation and thus a lack of true gnosis (Ma'rifah). This passage underscores the Shia theological emphasis on God's absolute incomparability (La Nadira), linking the failure to recognize divine transcendence with the Quranic narrative of followers disowning idols that were falsely elevated to divine status.
